glosses: To press forward; to advance by pushing.

examples.text: The man crowded into the packed room.

glosses: To press together or collect in numbers.

examples.text: They crowded through the archway and into the park.
[T]he whole company closed their ranks, and crowded about the fire.
Images came crowding on his mind faster than he could put them into words.

glosses: To press or drive together, especially into a small space; to cram.

examples.text: He tried to crowd too many cows into the cow-pen.
[…]The Time (miſ-order’d) doth in common ſence / Crowd vs, and cruſh vs, to this monſtrous Forme, / To hold our ſafetie vp.

glosses: To fill by pressing or thronging together

examples.text: The balconies and verandas were crowded with spectators, anxious to behold their future sovereign.

glosses: To push, to press, to shove.

examples.text: They tried to crowd her off the sidewalk.

glosses: To approach another ship too closely when it has right of way.
To carry excessive sail in the hope of moving faster.

examples.text: With all her might she crowds all sail off shore; in so doing, fights ’gainst the very winds that fain would blow her homeward; seeks all the lashed sea’s landlessness again; for refuge’s sake forlornly rushing into peril; her only friend her bitterest foe!

glosses: To press by solicitation; to urge; to dun; hence, to treat discourteously or unreasonably.
A group of people congregated or collected into a close body without order.

examples.text: After the movie let out, a crowd of people pushed through the exit doors.

glosses: Several things collected or closely pressed together; also, some things adjacent to each other.

examples.text: There was a crowd of toys pushed beneath the couch where the children were playing.

glosses: The so-called lower orders of people; the populace; the vulgar.
